name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelming
Chris Rabb has strong fundraising and outside support; independent rival is minimally funded
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: This Philadelphia seat carries a D+40 lean, and the Democratic nominee has outraised the independent challenger by more than 100-to-1 with substantial outside backing. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly well-funded late entrant could narrow the margin, though not the likely outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Dwight Evans's retirement leaves a heavily Democratic Philadelphia-area seat open, with state Rep. Chris Rabb the Democratic nominee and Dennis Mahoney running as an independent. The district's partisan lean of roughly D+40 makes a Democratic hold the strong default in any plausible environment.

Rabb has raised about $1.3 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside support, while Mahoney has raised about $11,000 with no outside spending. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 98%. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals and money, both of which point decisively to Rabb.
